correctness.rationale: For connected finite simple girth>=6 graphs N>=6, the bounded-independence dual Γ of the total 3-cut complex consists of all 0,1,2-sets; each 3-set with a graph edge; and each 4-set containing a 2-edge matching. Triangle-freeness and absence of 4-cycles ensure uniqueness of a matching; absence of 5-cycles plus R(3,3)=6 forbid faces of 5+ vertices. The dual for a spanning tree contracts by leaf deletion: the leaf link cones on its neighbor. When a chord ab is added, new 2-faces are abw outside B=N(a)∪N(b), new 3-faces are abxy for xy an edge of the remaining induced graph. Pair each new abw with abw p(w), where p(w) decreases distance to B, giving a relative acyclic matching. Unmatched 3-cells count |E(L)|−|V(L)\B|=old cycle rank+1. Attach b sequentially, no degree-2 attaching obstruction because previous wedge S³ is 2-connected; obtain Γ homotopy wedge binom(b+1,2) S³. Integral Alexander duality gives total cut reduced H only degree N−6, torsion-free rank binom(b+1,2), and purity dimension N−4 implies non-shellability for b>0. Direct independent GF2 boundary ranks: tree 0, C6 1, theta(3,3,3) 3; package code checks 1356 labelled n6 and nine cases including Heawood b8 rank36. Finite GF2 tests are not the integral proof.

originality.rationale: Bayer et al established tree and single-cycle total-cut cases, corresponding to b=0 and b=1; a published Heawood calculation gives rank36 at b=8 for a single graph. Carnero Bravo's full primary paper proves connectivity/vanishing bounds for Alexander duals at high girth, not the exact homotopy and quadratic cycle-rank multiplicity according to compared theorems. Ordinary (non-total) cut results have a different face condition. The new all-connected-high-girth edge-addition mechanism is not seen in compared prior claims, with residual chance of an unindexed generalization.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete all-cycle-ranks integral homology formula for a natural graph complex using just the graph's first Betti number, spanning all connected high-girth graphs including overlapping long cycles. The explicit relative Morse filtration yields a reusable structural mechanism and sharp torsion-free/non-shellable conclusions; this goes significantly beyond a single known Heawood or cycle tabulation.
